Amberg Synagogue

Synagogue · Amberg, Germany

The Amberg synagogue was created in 1896 when the Jewish community, with a donation from Baroness Clara von Hirsch, acquired and converted two adjoining houses on the Salzgasse into a house of worship, replacing a small prayer room used since 1881. The synagogue survived the Nazi era in its original location; after the war it was renovated and reopened to the returning Jewish community in August 1945. The Israelitische Kultusgemeinde Amberg, currently with about 125 members and led by Rabbi Elias Dray since 2013, continues to hold services in the same building, which has been repeatedly renovated and expanded, and offers regular public tours.
